newsitem.title: GERMANY: German 1996 magazine ad pages up one pct year/year.
newsitem.headline: German 1996 magazine ad pages up one pct year/year.

text.p: German magazines published 199,541 pages of advertising in 1996, up one percent from the year before, the German Magazine Publisher's Association (VDZ) said on Friday.

Citing a survey of 294 magazine titles, VDZ noted this was the third annual increase in a row after several years of falling advertising volume due to general shift in advertising towards electronic media.
It said car makers, financial services and the fashion industry spent more on print advertising than in the recent past.

VDZ said in a statement that it expected another increase in magazine advertising this year. The publishers group put magazine titles in the following order determined by the number of advertising pages sold. The list does not reflect advertising revenue. Percent changes compared with previous year.

VDZ said the most attractive genres were illustrated and news magazines, which published 25,000 pages of advertising, down 1.7 percent from the year before. Sports titles published 23,450 pages of advertising, up four percent.
The biggest growth segment was computer titles, which published 21,630 pages of advertising, up 15.1 percent.
